finding.title: Use a clock-skew-safe timestamp, not client clock, for notification_settings updated_at LWW field
finding.why: This client-computed timestamp becomes the payload's updated_at field pushed via enqueueNotificationSettings; core/sync/merge/notification_settings_merger.dart (outside this batch) parses remote['updated_at'] to arbitrate LWW. If two devices' clocks disagree, the device with the faster/wrong clock can push a stale settings change that looks 'newer' and wins over a genuinely newer change made on a correctly-clocked device, silently reverting the user's real edit with no error surfaced anywhere. Confirming the full blast radius requires reading the outbox-drain write path (outside this batch) to see whether it overwrites this field with FieldValue.serverTimestamp() before commit.
finding.recommendation: Confirm whether the write path already substitutes a server timestamp before commit; if not, do so, or route the push side through the same clock-skew arbitration MergeStore.remoteIsNewer already implements for the pull side.
acceptance_criteria: A sync test with an artificially-skewed local clock demonstrates the genuinely later settings write wins regardless of which device has the faster clock.

finding.title: Test the real _persistNotificationSettingsToCloud signature logic, not a hand-copied reimplementation
finding.why: _persistNotificationSettingsToCloud's M2 no-op-skip logic (skip pushing when the settings signature hasn't changed, to avoid bumping updated_at and clobbering a newer remote under LWW -- the exact mechanism the client-clock finding depends on) is a private function, so G1-G4 reimplement its string format by hand in the test file instead of exercising it. If a future edit to the real signature-building code drops a field or changes the separator, breaking the no-op-skip contract, G1-G4 keep passing because they never call the real function.
finding.recommendation: Extract the signature-building into an internal @visibleForTesting function the tests can call directly, or drive it end-to-end via notificationSettingsCloudSyncEffectProvider with a fake outbox facade asserting enqueue is/isn't called across setting changes.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation check confirms G1-G4 (or their replacement) fail when a field is removed from the real signature-building code in notification_providers.dart.

finding.title: Log-less catch blocks in notifications swallow exceptions with no AppLogger trail (EH-3)

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // Some tests build notification providers without full sync dependencies.

} catch (_) {
      // Timezone re-detection failed — keep existing tz.local.

} catch (_) {
      // Platform query failed — leave tz.local as UTC rather than crash.

finding.why: None of the three call AppLogger, so a real production failure is indistinguishable from the expected/benign case. The outbox-facade catch is the most consequential: it catches ANY exception from the whole outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider dependency chain -- not just the 'test doesn't override this provider' case its comment describes -- and silently disables cloud sync of notification settings for that session with zero diagnostic trail.
finding.recommendation: Log via AppLogger in all three; for the outbox-facade catch, narrow the caught condition so only the intended test-scaffolding case is swallowed and real errors are logged/propagated distinctly.
acceptance_criteria: Each catch gains a corresponding AppLogger call.
A grep for catch (_) { or catch (e) { in lib/features/notifications without a following AppLogger call in the same block fails CI.

finding.title: Construct StreakAlertService only through its @riverpod provider (SM-7)
finding.why: streakAlertServiceProvider is locked to activeProfileIdProvider's profile, so allProfilesReminderBootstrap, which must handle every inactive profile, can't use it and hand-constructs a second instance instead. A test that overrides streakAlertServiceProvider with a fake has no effect on inactive-profile scheduling, and any future required dependency added to StreakAlertService's constructor must be kept in sync by hand at both call sites.
finding.recommendation: Convert to a family-style provider parameterized by profileId and use it at both call sites.
acceptance_criteria: A test overriding the family provider for a specific inactive profileId observably changes allProfilesReminderBootstrap's behavior for that profile.

finding.title: Replace hardcoded hex Color literals with AppColors tokens in notifications UI
finding.why: Both files already import and correctly use AppColors/AppTheme for some colors, so the raw hex values are avoidable inconsistency, not a missing token system. A future theme change (dark mode, rebrand) requires hunting these two files for magic hex values instead of touching one theme file, and this violates the (currently non-enforcing, due to the custom_lint breakage) no_color_literal_outside_theme rule.
finding.recommendation: Promote the repeated literals to named AppColors tokens and reference those instead of inline Color(0x...) values.
acceptance_criteria: Once custom_lint is fixed (tracked separately), dart run custom_lint reports zero no_color_literal_outside_theme hits in lib/features/notifications/.
